extracted.intended_audience: potential grantees, partners, donors, job seekers, and the general public interested in The Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational 'About Us' page describing the Trust's mission, history, program priorities, leadership, team composition, financial transparency, and grantmaking scope. Useful for understanding what the Trust funds and how it presents itself to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in new ideas or research across six program areas: Crohn’s Disease, Israel, Rural Healthcare, Type 1 Diabetes, Vulnerable Children in Sub-Saharan Africa, and New York City.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists these six program areas as the focus of the Trust's investments and grantmaking. Use these areas to assess alignment of proposals or partnership ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority: unmet needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support programs that address unmet needs, particularly noted in the Type 1 Diabetes program which is described as 'built on funding unmet needs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on filling gaps rather than duplicating existing efforts; proposals that address clear unmet needs may align with the Trust's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership and collaboration emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Helmsley 'partners with people and organizations' and the Type 1 Diabetes Program 'works closely with partners in private philanthropy, industry, academia, and government.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust favors collaborative approaches and cross-sector partnerships; applicants should demonstrate partnership strategies and roles for collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope and targeted geographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a 'global philanthropy' that works 'across the U.S. and select parts of the world' with specific program foci including New York City and Sub-Saharan Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While global in orientation, the Trust has targeted geographic priorities; applicants should confirm whether their region/program aligns with the Trust's geographic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust posts its latest balance sheet and Form 990-PF and provides charts of total assets and charitable disbursements dating back to Fiscal Year 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of financial statements and 990-PFs signals institutional transparency and long-term capacity; potential grantees and partners can review these documents to understand funding scale and history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team expertise and lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The team is 'a diverse group of people who have expertise and often very personal experience' including innovators, engineers, scientists, social workers, public health and mental health experts, educators, philanthropists, and people personally affected by Crohn’s or Type 1 Diabetes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust values both technical expertise and lived experience; proposals demonstrating subject-matter expertise and inclusion of affected communities may be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustee qualifications and leadership background
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustees have professional and personal backgrounds relevant to the Trust's work (e.g., legal, personal experience with Type 1 Diabetes, first-responder experience highlighting rural health disparities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership biographies indicate the perspectives that inform funding decisions; understanding trustee interests can help tailor proposals and engagement approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantmaking history, scale, and institutional capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Active grantmaking since 2008 with an $8 billion endowment; the Trust describes growth from a start-up to a global philanthropy working with organizations across sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust's long-term grantmaking history and large endowment imply capacity for multi-year and sizable investments; applicants should consider appropriate scale and sustainability in requests.
